### Description

This code is pretty straightforward:
```python
import jax.numpy as jnp
import jax.random as jr
import jax.lax as jl
import jax

a = jr.normal(jr.PRNGKey(1), (15000, 1000)).astype(jnp.bfloat16)
b = jr.normal(jr.PRNGKey(2), (1000, 15000)).astype(jnp.bfloat16)
r = jl.dot(a, b, preferred_element_type=jnp.float32)
jax.block_until_ready(r)
```
This code takes around 6 seconds to complete on RTX 3090, but when you add ```precision=jax.lax.Precision.HIGH```
it will take only 2.3 seconds.

When you replace 15000 with 20000 this code will try to allocate 24Gb of RAM and simply OOM, while higher precision works just fine. What happens inside of JAX when it tries to execute it?

### What jax/jaxlib version are you using?

jax 0.4.13, jaxlib 0.4.13+cuda12.cudnn89

### Which accelerator(s) are you using?

GPU - RTX 3090, Tesla A100

Ubuntu 22.10
